functions.name: find
functions.signature: find(bmp: Bytes, min-area: U64) -> Result[Bytes, Text]

semantics: grey8 A2 input only (a bgra8 input is unsupported-format); foreground = pixel value >= 128; a region is a maximal 4-connected (left/right/up/down) foreground component, emitted as the closed external region's bounding box {x=min_x, y=min_y, w=max_x-min_x+1, h=max_y-min_y+1}; a region is emitted iff its foreground pixel area >= min-area (inclusive filter, not a parameter-accept gate); ordering is by the row-major seed (lowest (y,x)); list<region> is A1-encoded as count u32 LE then count x 16 B (x,y,width,height u32 LE); no qualifying region is a count-0 ok.
semantics-provenance: The connection rule (4-connectivity), foreground threshold (>= 128), bounding-box region form and the min-area filter are RFC-0043 §A4-DELEGATED internal reference semantics for the `image-contour@1` op — §A4 hands each op's exact behavior to 'the determinism rules + the content-asserting corpus', so the frozen corpus (not an owner wire ruling) is the authority here. This is NOT a cross-boundary wire contract: the cross-boundary shapes ARE owner-ruled and already frozen — input framing by RFC-0043-A2 and list<region> result encoding by RFC-0043-A1. Same delegation basis as image-grid's detect-lines (STEP-0336).

refusal-corpus.source: independent oracle (pure-stdlib Python, no shared code with the dependency-free Rust core)

unreachable-image-error.reason: bounding regions derive from within-image components and can never exceed the raster; asserted absent in-test
